findings.summary: crates/app/src/main.rs fetch(): no test covers the ureq request deadline (timeout_global(Some(GIVE_UP))). A mutant with timeout_global(None) passes every test. In the held-connection e2e it leaked a thread and a socket per unanswered read: threads went 24 to 26 and 2 connections were left ESTABLISHED. Only the e2e shows the deadline matters.

crates/app/tests/board.rs: no test covers the stale line's wrapping. Replacing .wrap() with .truncate() still passes needs_you_is_listed_first_and_cards_show_their_gate_and_pr. Wrapping was observed live in a 1200 px window (10-narrow.png).

A restarted server whose first GitHub read fails says 'github is stale (no good read yet): ... (kept its PRs from an earlier read)', but it has no earlier read and shows no PRs (08strip.png, 10-narrow.png). The suffix should depend on there being earlier data.

AC-7 names the cluster, but the server has no cluster source yet (only linear and github), so that part is unexercised. AC-6's 'PR checks finish within 2 minutes' holds only with GITHUB_TOKEN. Tokenless, GitHub reads were 27 min apart (16:28:38, then 16:55:18); docs/STATUS.md says so.
